prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures the close-quarters layout of an unfinished wooden structure where the camera wearer (torso and outstretched left arm visible at the bottom at 0.2–0.5 m) holds the near underside of a large plastic-wrapped fixture (0.3–1.2 m away) containing a recessed rectangular box. In frames 1 and 2, a second person ahead and above at the top edge (roughly 1.5–2.0 m away, facing toward the fixture and camera wearer with their head cropped out of view) and a third person to the lower left (roughly 1.0–1.5 m away) are both within arm's reach of the fixture's edges, ~1.0–1.5 m from the wearer and ~1.5 m from each other. Across frames 1 to 5, the fixture rotates and shifts upward and rightward relative to the camera wearer, moving the upper person out of view by frame 3 while the wearer's right arm enters at the bottom right in frames 4–5 at ~0.3 m. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map makes the 3D protrusion of the internal cardboard box through the translucent plastic wrap and the receding depth plane of the left-hand wooden studs much clearer. However, the depth map is unreliable across the translucent plastic sheet—smoothing over the hollow cavity inside the fixture rather than representing the wrap and interior surfaces separately—and flattens the background ceiling beams into dark, indistinct regions.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only a few fragmentary regions of the scene: the upper coworker in frames 1–2 (0.8–1.2 m beyond the near rim of the fixture), the main body of the plastic-wrapped fixture in frames 3–5 (0.3–1.2 m in front of and above the camera wearer), and the wearer's own right forearm entering at the bottom right in frames 4–5 (~0.3 m away). In frames 1 and 2, the upper person's torso and right arm are segmented at the top center (facing toward the fixture and camera wearer, head cropped out of frame, hands touching the far edge), while in frames 3–5 the large fixture mask clearly carves out a silhouette around the camera wearer's unsegmented left hand resting on its near rim within arm's reach (~0.4 m). Across the 5 frames, the upper person's mask shrinks and exits the top edge as the fixture advances and rotates clockwise, after which the large fixture mask and the wearer's right-arm mask appear. While the segmentation map sharply delineates the boundary where the wearer's left hand occludes the fixture in frames 3–5, it provides almost no spatial information that is not already obvious in the RGB strip. It is highly unreliable overall: it completely misses the fixture in frames 1–2, misclassifies the plastic-wrapped fixture as an "umbrella" in frames 3–5, fails to segment the camera wearer's torso and left arm or the lower-left person in frames 1–2, and omits the surrounding walls and internal cardboard box entirely.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost completely blank across all five frames, detecting only a single distorted yellow body skeleton in the lower-left region of frame 2 where the camera wearer's chest and outstretched left arm (0.2–0.5 m from the camera) overlap near the lower-left coworker (1.0–1.5 m away). It provides no spatial layout for the surrounding wooden framing or the large fixture in front of the camera wearer, and detects no skeletons at all in frames 1, 3, 4, or 5. Because of severe self-occlusion from the egocentric viewpoint and heavy cropping of the other people at the frame boundaries, the map fails to indicate which way anyone is facing, whether anyone looks toward the camera wearer, or how the participants move and rotate across the sequence. Furthermore, no magenta hand skeletons are detected in any frame despite the camera wearer's left hand being clearly visible in the foreground within ~0.4 m across all five frames and their right arm entering in frames 4–5. Consequently, the pose map adds no useful spatial detail beyond the RGB image and is unreliable for tracking either full bodies or hands under this steep, close-range viewing angle.
